- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–8% for 3–7 day horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 10–20%.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 1–2 day mean-reversion buffer toward prior 10-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price volatility; increase forecast by 1–3% for high-sentiment periods or when true outcome shows >10% deviation from 10-day moving average.
- When sentiment is high and price is near support level, model tends to ignore support; add a 1–2 day “support ceiling” rule: cap forecast at 5–10% below recent low if sentiment >0.7.
